basis: Pectoral muscle and hand defects define syndrome; subcutaneous tissue absence occurs in 80-99%, renal hypoplasia in 30-79%; cardiac anomalies are occasional.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: absence of subcutaneous fat in 80-99% represents structural tissue loss; subcutis belongs to this axis.

basis: Corticospinal and peripheral nerve disease; distal amyotrophy in 9/11 is secondary to denervation, without evidence of direct muscle pathology.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: amyotrophy in 9/11 is neurogenic; denervation-related muscle wasting does not establish direct muscle involvement.

basis: Immune dysregulation with eosinophilia; dermatitis 4/4 supports skin involvement. Colonic eosinophilia 1/1 and food allergy do not establish common damaging gut disease.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: food allergy does not establish intestinal damage; colonic eosinophilia in one assessed patient establishes neither dysfunction nor prevalence of at least 30%.

basis: Craniofacial and ocular duplication define disease; anencephaly and cardiac septal abnormalities each 80-99%. Cleft palate, also 80-99%, omitted at four-axis cap.

decisions.ocular: primary: ocular duplication is part of the defining facial malformation, with eye and visual abnormalities annotated in 80-99%.

basis: Arterial and skeletal disease define LDS1; exotropia in 2/4 supports ocular dysfunction, with limited sampling. Bifid uvula, soft skin and blue sclerae alone do not establish damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: bifid uvula is a diagnostic structural marker without established oral dysfunction; it does not establish gastrointestinal damage.
decisions.ocular: involved: exotropia in 2/4 assessed patients supports persistent ocular misalignment at approximately 50%; confidence is limited by the small denominator.

basis: Alport nephropathy, sensorineural deafness and esophageal leiomyomatosis define syndrome; cataract occurs in 3/4. Airway leiomyomatosis is occasional (<30%).

decisions.otologic: primary: sensorineural deafness is explicitly part of the defining Alport phenotype, with HPO frequency 30-79%.

basis: Short metacarpals and insulin resistance define syndrome; spherocytosis is explicitly described and annotated 80-99%, supporting a primary blood-cell axis. Congestion is insufficient.

decisions.haematologic: primary: spherocytosis is an intrinsic blood-cell abnormality described in the syndrome and annotated 80-99%; the haematologic mechanism axis applies.

basis: Spastic paraplegia and polyneuropathy with destructive acropathy and terminal digit loss define disease; structural skeletal involvement exceeds weakness or gait symptoms.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: acropathy with loss of terminal digits is explicitly defining structural damage, supported by frequent knee and Achilles abnormalities (30-79%).

basis: Radial reduction and anorectal/urethral malformations define syndrome; hydrocephalus occurs in 80-99%. Hypospadias affects the urethra, within the renal axis.

decisions.renal: primary: hypospadias is a defining urethral malformation; the renal axis explicitly includes the urethra.

basis: Dystroglycan glycosylation disorder defined by progressive muscular dystrophy and intellectual disability; severe intellectual disability is frequent (30-79%).

decisions.neurologic: primary: intellectual disability is explicitly part of the defining phenotype, with severe disability annotated in 30-79%.
